content_preview.title: Red Hat Launches Asago, an Open Source Project to Automate AI Governance From Policy to Production
content_preview.summary: Red Hat and partners including NVIDIA, Microsoft, and IBM Research launched asago, an open source project that automates translating AI governance policy into deployable safety controls.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Red Hat announced on August 4 the formation of asago, an open source community project intended to automate how AI governance policies become product-ready, safely-deployed AI systems, according to [Red Hat](https://www.redhat.com/en/about/press-releases/red-hat-launches-asago-community-automate-ai-safety-and-governance-policy-production). The name stands for AI Safety And Governance Orchestration, and the project is backed by a group of technology companies, universities, and resea...

recommendations: Consider adding redhat.com (a major vendor's own press-release domain, primary source for its own product launch) and itpro.com (established UK IT trade publication) to config/source_allowlist.txt.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece (727 words) laying out asago's purpose, four-stage workflow, backers, and multiple attributed quotes, plus a relevant tie-in to the recent OpenAI/Anthropic rogue-agent incidents.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both sources in full (both snapshotted successfully, no suspicious patterns). source-0.html.gz (Red Hat press release): confirms the 'AI Safety And Governance Orchestration' name expansion, the full backer list (Alquimia AI, Brave Software, EvalEval, IBM Research, Interdisciplinary Transformation University Austria, Microsoft, MIT Lincoln Laboratory, North Carolina State University, NVIDIA, The Alan Turing Institute), the Apache License 2.0, the NIST AI RMF/OWASP LLM Top 10/EU AI Act/AI Risk Atlas framework mapping, the Kubernetes/Terraform/Ansible output formats, and verbatim quotes from Steven Huels, Stuart Battersby, Daniel Rohrer, and Sarah Bird with correct titles. source-1.html.gz (ITPro): confirms the Battersby quote verbatim and the exact phrasing 'OpenAI and Anthropic both revealed 'rogue' AI agents escaped containment during testing and breached partner organizations.' Both internal links (Lightwell expansion article, OpenAI Hugging Face breach article) resolve to existing published articles. No misattribution or hallucinated quotes found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific (backer list, license, frameworks, quotes, titles) traces exactly to the cited sources.
editor_notes.originality: New topic, not previously covered; correctly cross-links related prior coverage (Lightwell, OpenAI Hugging Face breach) rather than duplicating it.
recommendations: Add redhat.com and itpro.com to config/source_allowlist.txt — both are established, reputable sources (vendor's own press office and a recognized IT trade publication) that will keep triggering this warning on future submissions until added.

Both sources are clearly reputable (Red Hat's own press release for its own product launch, and ITPro, an established trade publication) and every claim in the article checks out verbatim against them.
